name: gutenberg
description: Project Gutenberg, a free public-domain eBook library. This CLI reads book details, lists books by author, subject, reading list or category, shows the top-downloaded and newly posted books, finds related books, and downloads plain text and RDF metadata.

commands.name: get-book
commands.summary: Get one eBook's detail page: title, summary, the bibliographic table (author, subjects, language, release date, downloads) and the author link

fields.title: h1#book_title
fields.author_url: a[title='Find more eBooks by the same author.']@href
fields.author_label: a[title='Find more eBooks by the same author.']

commands.name: list-author-books
commands.summary: List the eBooks by one author (25 per page), sorted by popularity, title or release date

params.name: author_id
params.description: Gutenberg author id, e.g. 69 for Arthur Conan Doyle. Get it from get-book's author_url.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. Popularity is the default when omitted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.name: list-subject-books
commands.summary: List the eBooks under a Library-of-Congress-style subject (25 per page)

params.name: subject_id
params.description: Gutenberg subject id, e.g. 76 for 'Holmes, Sherlock (Fictitious character) -- Fiction'

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. Popularity is the default when omitted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.name: list-bookshelf-books
commands.summary: List the eBooks on a reading list (bookshelf) or in a main category (25 per page)

params.name: bookshelf_id
params.description: Bookshelf or category id, e.g. 30 = Detective Fiction, 638 = a main category. Get ids from list-bookshelves, list-categories or search-bookshelves.

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. The UI offers 'title' and 'author' (popularity is the default when omitted); 'release_date' and 'downloads' are likely also accepted.

params.name: start_index
params.description: 1-based index of the first result. Pages are 25 items: 1, 26, 51, …

commands.name: list-bookshelves
commands.summary: List all volunteer-curated reading lists (bookshelves) A–Z with their links

commands.name: search-bookshelves
commands.summary: Find reading lists and categories whose names match keywords (use | to OR several terms)

params.name: query
params.description: Keyword(s); separate alternatives with '|', e.g. crime|detective|mystery

params.name: sort_order
params.description: Sort order. The UI offers Quantity and Title; popularity is the default when omitted.

commands.name: list-categories
commands.summary: List the main subject categories (Literature, Science & Technology, History, …) with their bookshelf links

commands.name: get-top-downloads
commands.summary: Top 100 most-downloaded eBooks and authors for yesterday, the last 7 days and the last 30 days

commands.name: list-also-downloaded
commands.summary: Books that readers of a given eBook also downloaded (related books)

commands.name: get-book-text
commands.summary: Download the full plain-text (UTF-8) content of an eBook

commands.name: get-book-rdf
commands.summary: Get an eBook's machine-readable RDF/XML catalog metadata (title, creators, subjects, formats), converted to JSON

commands.name: list-new-books
commands.summary: eBooks posted or updated today (RSS feed of new releases)

commands.name: list-featured-books
commands.summary: The home page shelves: about 10 newest releases followed by about 10 most popular books

notes: Keyword search of books (/ebooks/search/ and /ebooks/search.opds/) is blocked by robots.txt and is not available. To find books, start from list-categories, search-bookshelves, list-bookshelves, get-top-downloads or list-new-books, then follow the ids.
Book urls look like /ebooks/{id}. The number after /ebooks/ is the id that get-book, list-also-downloaded, get-book-text and get-book-rdf take.
Author ids come from get-book's author_url (/ebooks/author/{id}). Bookshelf and category ids come from /ebooks/bookshelf/{id} links.
List pages return 25 results. Paging uses start_index = 1, 26, 51, … and the last page has fewer than 25 items.

get-top-downloads returns all ranking lists concatenated, in page order: top books yesterday, top authors yesterday, top books last 7 days, top authors last 7 days, top books last 30 days, top authors last 30 days. Each block holds up to 100 entries. Book entries link to /ebooks/{id}, author entries link to /browse/authors/....
list-featured-books returns both home-page shelves in one list: New Releases first, then Most Popular.
The download counts in list results are text such as '99027 downloads'.
get-book-text can be very large (the whole book). Other formats can be fetched directly at /ebooks/{id}.epub3.images, .epub.images, .epub.noimages, .kf8.images and .kindle.images.

Bulk catalog data: plain-text indexes at /dirs/GUTINDEX.ALL (or per year, /dirs/GUTINDEX.{year}) and full RDF/CSV metadata under /cache/epub/feeds/, both described at /ebooks/offline_catalogs.html. Project Gutenberg asks automated users not to crawl the site heavily.
